 Jaguar recalls over 93K Range Rovers due to water pooling around rearview camera
 By Daniel Miller FOX Local Recalls Published  October 28, 2026 10:47 AM EDT Share
 Copy Link 
 Email 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 LinkedIn 
 Reddit 
 Published  October 28, 2026 10:47 AM EDT article FILE-A logo is pictured outside a Jaguar Land Rover dealership on May 24, 2020. (Photo by BEN STANSALL/AFP via Getty Images) 
 The Brief
 2022-2026MY Land Rover Range Rover vehicles were recalled connected to a water issue that can impact the rearview camera. 
 The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said that if the image is affected on the rearview camera, this could increase crash risk.  
 Owners of the recalled vehicles can receive free repairs at their local dealerships.  
 Jaguar Land Rover issued a voluntary recall of 93,997 Range Rovers linked to a water management system issue with the vehicles that may prevent water from adequately draining from the rearview camera. 
 National Highway Traffic Safety Administration officials explained in   a recall letter that when "water pools around the rearview camera" installation, over time, this may cause damage to the camera and result in a distorted image, or no image at all, to be displayed on the vehicle’s touchscreen.
 RELATED: Toyota recalls over 500K vehicles due to instrument panel issues 
 The federal safety agency added that a   blurred image or lack of display of the rearview camera   image could lead to a driver being unaware of objects or pedestrians, raising the risk of an injury or a crash.
 To date, there have been no reported accidents, injuries or fires related to the recalled Range Rovers. 
 Which Range Rover models were recalled?
 Why you should care:
 The recall covers certain   2022-2026MY Land Rover Range Rover   vehicles manufactured between July 08, 2021, and June 04, 2026. 
 Are repairs available for the recalled Range Rovers?
 What you can do:
 Owners of the affected Range Rovers can receive free repairs on their vehicles. 
 According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the vehicles will have extra drain holes drilled in the "underside of the tailgate trim," which contains the camera. Additionally, the functionality of the camera will be verified and, if necessary, it will be replaced. 
 Owner notification letters will be distributed on or before Dec. 11. 
 The Source: Information for this story was provided by a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recall letter. This story was reported from Washington, D.C.
